title: Calculus-based Physics 2
introduction: Study oscillations, waves, fields, circuits and electromagnetic radiation through models, calculations and checked evidence. The first three of 31 planned lessons are available: harmonic motion; energy, physical oscillators and stable equilibrium; and free decay and damping regimes. The remaining lessons, module and cumulative assessments, and sustained simulation project are under construction. This proposed self-study sequence preserves the academic physics and calculus prerequisites; it is not an NU course or credit award.

lessons.title: Harmonic motion, phase and initial conditions
lessons.objective: Reconstruct and check a harmonic trajectory from physical parameters or initial conditions, including phase, direction and admissible event times.

lessons.title: Energy, physical oscillators and stable equilibrium
lessons.objective: Derive a local oscillation model from force, torque or potential energy and assess its frequency and small-amplitude limits.

lessons.title: Free decay and damping regimes
lessons.objective: Classify and solve a damped oscillator's initial-value response and distinguish amplitude, energy and settling measures.

lessons.title: Driven response, resonance and power transfer
lessons.objective: Predict a driven oscillator's steady amplitude, phase and average power while separating transient behavior and distinct resonance criteria.

lessons.title: Wave functions and transport of energy
lessons.objective: Interpret a traveling wave's direction, local motion and energy transport using its derivatives and medium parameters.

lessons.title: Superposition, reflection and normal modes
lessons.objective: Construct superposed waves that satisfy boundary conditions and identify their nodes, allowed modes and energy behavior.

lessons.title: Sound, intensity and moving sources
lessons.objective: Relate pressure waves and sound measurements to intensity, interference and relative source-observer motion within a stated medium.

lessons.title: Charge, force and the electric field
lessons.objective: Calculate signed vector electric forces and fields from discrete sources and distinguish source properties from the response of a test charge.

lessons.title: Fields of continuous charge distributions
lessons.objective: Set up and evaluate electric-field integrals with correct density, geometry, vector direction and admissible observation points.

lessons.title: Electric flux and the proper use of Gauss's law
lessons.objective: Calculate oriented flux and use Gauss's law to determine a field only when the source symmetry supports the required reduction.

lessons.title: Conductors, cavities and electrostatic boundaries
lessons.objective: Determine charge allocation and field constraints in electrostatic conductors while distinguishing metal, cavities and surrounding space.

lessons.title: Potential, work and field reconstruction
lessons.objective: Connect electrostatic field and potential through line integrals and gradients, retaining reference choices and source-domain restrictions.

lessons.title: Capacitance, networks and stored energy
lessons.objective: Determine capacitance, charge, voltage and energy for specified geometries and connected capacitors, with topology and source conditions explicit.

lessons.title: Dielectrics and electromechanical energy accounting
lessons.objective: Predict a capacitor's response to dielectric or geometry changes by distinguishing fixed charge, fixed voltage and the work of external sources.

lessons.title: Current density, resistance and material response
lessons.objective: Relate charge transport to current, local fields, resistance and heating while identifying the limits of an ohmic material model.

lessons.title: DC circuit constraints and instrument loading
lessons.objective: Solve a DC network with signed current and voltage references, verify power balance, and predict how a real meter changes the circuit.

lessons.title: RC switching, initial conditions and time scales
lessons.objective: Derive and check a first-order circuit transient with a specified pre-switch state, final value and admissible switching model.

lessons.title: Lorentz force and charged-particle motion
lessons.objective: Predict charged-particle force and trajectory in specified uniform fields with consistent vector signs and energy reasoning.

lessons.title: Currents, magnetic dipoles and material models
lessons.objective: Calculate force, torque and energy for current-carrying conductors and magnetic dipoles while identifying the assumptions of simple material models.

lessons.title: Biot-Savart, Ampere's law and magnetic geometry
lessons.objective: Compute magnetostatic fields from currents and justify when a circulation law can determine their spatial dependence.

lessons.title: Changing flux and induced electric fields
lessons.objective: Calculate signed induced emf for a specified circuit and distinguish transformer induction, motional emf and electrostatic potential difference.

lessons.title: Inductance, coupled coils and RL transients
lessons.objective: Relate current to flux linkage, stored magnetic energy and inductive voltage, including mutual coupling and initial-value circuit behavior.

lessons.title: Generators, transformers and transmission losses
lessons.objective: Build a power account for idealized generators and transformers and evaluate the assumptions behind voltage conversion and reduced line losses.

lessons.title: Sinusoids, phasors and impedance
lessons.objective: Translate between time-domain sinusoids and complex phasors to solve a linear sinusoidal circuit with consistent amplitude and phase conventions.

lessons.title: Electrical oscillation and resonance evidence
lessons.objective: Relate free LC/RLC transients to driven resonance and interpret the measured response, damping and bandwidth for a specified output.

lessons.title: Average power, RMS and power factor
lessons.objective: Compute real energy transfer and distinguish it from reactive exchange and apparent power under stated waveform and reference conditions.

lessons.title: Maxwell's equations and charge continuity
lessons.objective: Use integral field laws to check charge continuity and displacement current, and interpret their local differential forms with stated material assumptions.

lessons.title: Electromagnetic wave solutions and polarization
lessons.objective: Construct a plane electromagnetic wave consistent with Maxwell's equations and interpret its direction, polarization and medium-dependent speed.

lessons.title: Field energy, intensity and radiation pressure
lessons.objective: Account for energy and momentum carried by electromagnetic waves and distinguish local fields, average intensity and material interaction models.

modules.title: Numerical evidence and a sustained investigation

lessons.title: Numerical field and circuit checks
lessons.objective: Evaluate a numerical physical prediction using independent representations, refinement and explicit numerical-versus-measurement uncertainty.

lessons.title: Investigate a resonant circuit model
lessons.objective: Design, analyze and report a reproducible simulation investigation that distinguishes competing resonant-circuit models using calibrated observations and independent energy checks.
